verdicts.citation: SPEC.md 6.1 'Size on screen' [D]: 'One grid unit is u=min(64, floor((W-16)/k)) CSS pixels, where W is the width of the board's box ... On a viewport narrower than 400 pixels the box runs from edge to edge of the viewport, so W is the viewport width. The hit area of a node is a square of side min(44,u)'. 7.5 A-7: 'In a box 320 pixels wide this gives 44 for boards with at most six nodes in a row, 43 for seven (E8), 38 for eight'. decisions/P0-A5.md '2026-10-10 P0-A5: size rule and the reserved box' takes W from the figure, which runs edge to edge. Both support the finding's expected.
verdicts.evidence: Read 6.1 whole (both [D] paragraphs), 7.5 A-7, 4.0 'Small screens', 8.1 P11 and CONTRACTS 5.1 ('Hit area min(44, u) per 6.1'), all at 006f50d. The 6.1 [D] text fixes W as the viewport width below 400, with no qualifier. A-7's 'where the layout allows' points to that same rule ('The rule is in section 6.1') and to the 320 values it gives. DECISIONS.md / decisions/P0-A5.md records the build's reading: 'the board's grid unit is computed in CSS from the width of the figure, which is an inline-size container ... Below 400 pixels the figure runs from edge to edge of the viewport'. Board.svelte's comment at the gate says the same ('the nearest inline-size container, the tool's figure'). T12RepresentationBuilder.svelte at the gate gives `.panel` `padding: 8px 12px; border: 1px solid ...; container-type: inline-size`, and `.board-host` sits inside `section.panel.string`, so the nearest container is the panel, not the figure. decisions/P5-A2.md has no entry on the string viewer's size or container. The only record of the panel as a size container is decisions/P3-A5.md 'the stacking width and the layout boxes', and it covers T7 only. build-plan/reports/orchestrator/phase5/P5-A2-review.json notes '39 px on E8 and D8 and 34 px on B8 (A-7 lists 43 and 38 for a 320 px box), because the board sits inside the panel's padding'. That is a review note, not a decision, an owner's answer or an open item. reports/gate-G5.md (from claude/session-6a181f60-hzzoud; it names 006f50d as the gate commit) lists no open item on hit areas. Lens file section 6 excludes only sub-pixel deviations and widths of 400 and above. The deviation here is 4 to 5 px, at 320 and 360. T12 is phase 5 (SPEC 4 'T12. Representation Builder (phase 5)') and the gate is G5.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 fails because 6.1 sets W to the viewport width below 400 with no qualifier, and A-7's 'where the layout allows' refers back to that rule; R2 fails because expected quotes 6.1 and A-7 correctly; R3 fails because T12 is phase 5 at gate G5; R4 does not apply (no oracle quantity); R5 fails because 6.1 is [D] but the build departs from its text, P0-A5 records the figure as W, and the panel-as-container record (P3-A5) covers only T7; R6 fails because the P5-A2 review note is neither an open item in gate-G5.md nor a tracked finding. Major matches 'a behaviour the specification states is ... wrong'.

verdicts.citation: SPEC.md 7.5 A-1: 'Every tool is fully operable from the keyboard ...' (criteria 2.1.1, 2.1.2, 2.1.4, 2.4.3), under the 7.5 target 'WCAG 2.2 level AA'. 4.0 'Keyboard and screen reader'. The precedents P3-RT-05-09 and P4-RT-05-01 were confirmed under A-1 / 2.4.3 for focus dropped to <body>. The text supports the finding's expected.
verdicts.evidence: Read 7.5 A-1 and A-2, 4.0 'Works before and without JavaScript' ('Controls are present but disabled until the island has hydrated') and 7.4 'Without JavaScript' ('Controls are rendered with the disabled attribute, which the island removes when it hydrates'). Neither sentence covers a scroll box, and neither permits the focus to be dropped at hydration. decisions/P5-A2.md 'MatrixView' makes the server's scroll box 'a tab stop with a name, A-11', so it can take the focus before hydration. 'hydration (review finding 4, request 10)' records that 'A drawn MatrixView takes over the server's table (adopt)' and that the panels are drawn again after hydration (activate). Nothing there mentions focus. At the gate, MatrixView.svelte creates a new `<div class="box" tabindex="0" role="group">` and `moveIn` appends only the adopted `<table>`, and goLive/activate replace the parts, which matches the claim. DECISIONS.md: RT-FIX-P3-follow-predict and RT-FIX-P4-a11y keep the focus on controls their own press makes inactive. Those entries say nothing about hydration, and no entry permits losing focus. reports/gate-G5.md has no open item on focus. No `// regression:` test covers hydration. T12 and M8 are phase 5 and the gate is G5. The P4 round kept P4-RT-05-01 (same symptom) at major, with no adjustment.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 fails because 4.0 and 7.4 disable controls before hydration but say nothing that permits dropping a focused scroll box's focus; R2 fails because the finding cites A-1 and its 2.4.3 criterion as the project's precedents read them; R3 fails because T12 and M8 are phase 5 at gate G5; R4 does not apply; R5 fails because 7.5 is not [D] and P5-A2's hydration entry records the swap but no focus rule; R6 fails because nothing is on record. Major matches the precedent P4-RT-05-01 and 'a behaviour the specification states is missing'.

verdicts.citation: SPEC.md 4.0 [D] 'Keyboard and screen reader': '... a polite live region announces each result with the wording fixed in section 7.5'. 4.0 'Test hooks' names 'a verdict' among a tool's outputs. 7.5 target WCAG 2.2 AA (4.1.3). The 4.0 sentence supports the finding. A-4 itself governs moves, so it is a weaker part of the specRef, but the cause stands on 4.0.
verdicts.evidence: Read 4.0 whole, 7.5 A-4 ('Each move is announced ...') and CONTRACTS 5.3 (move templates only). The relation verdict is a result: the build announces it itself when the list is on the main thread. At the gate, model.ts relationSentence returns `${text}: the two sides are ${check.holds ? 'equal' : 'not equal'}.` and pickRelation calls announce(...). The `(check === null)` branch gives `${text}: checked in the background.`. acceptFromWorker in T12RepresentationBuilder.svelte (about lines 607 to 631 at 006f50d) stores the list, may move tool.relation through failingDefault, and redraws the sides, with no announce call. The verdict span `data-out="relation-verdict"` is not inside a live region (grep: no aria-live or role=status in T12). decisions/P5-A2.md 'where each call runs' and 'main-thread work of the relation list' send the list to the worker above RELATIONS_MAIN_WORK. They record nothing about announcing, or not announcing, the reply. DECISIONS.md 'MERGE: P5 stage 5.2' and 'MERGE: P5 stages 5.2 and 5.3 repaired after review' hold no such entry, and the owner-held phase 5 items concern E-9 sizing only. reports/gate-G5.md has no open item. Lens file section 6 excludes recorded plan readings 'where A-4 is silent' only when they are recorded; this omission is not. The P4 round kept P4-RT-05-05 (a silent Check) at major.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 fails because no sentence lets a result go unannounced when it comes from the worker; R2 fails in substance because 4.0 'announces each result' carries the claim, even though A-4 governs moves; R3 fails because T12 is phase 5 at gate G5; R4 does not apply; R5 fails because 4.0 is [D] but the build departs from 'announces each result', and no fragment records the omission; R6 fails because nothing is on record. Major matches 'a message missing'; it is not 'a tool not announced', since moves and picks are announced.

verdicts.citation: SPEC.md 7.5 A-4: 'Each move is announced through one polite live region per tool ... Templates, with negative numbers spoken as "minus": "Fired node 3. ..."; "Mutated city 2. ..."; ... "Undid move 4. Numbers now ..."'. The 'spoken as minus' rule qualifies the move templates, and a relation pick or a node pick is not a move. 7.5 A-12: 'Mathematics is rendered with MathML available to assistive technology (KaTeX's default output)' governs rendering, which the build meets: decisions/P5-A2.md '2026-10-24 P5-A2: the relation in MathML'. The explanation's wording is a logged decision under the [D] heading of 4.0: decisions/P5-A2.md '2026-10-24 P5-A2: the verdict and the explanation (F11)'.
verdicts.evidence: The only place 'spoken' or 'minus' appears as a rule in SPEC at 006f50d is A-4, attached to 'Templates' of moves (grep of SPEC for spoken, "minus" and screen reader). CONTRACTS 5.3 'exact strings of SPEC.md 7.5' lists only the move templates and the stated limits. CONTRACTS 4 gives speak() as a function, not as a rule for every sentence. 4.0 [D] says the region 'announces each result with the wording fixed in section 7.5'. 7.5 fixes no wording for a relation pick or a node pick, so that wording is the builder's. The finding concedes this: its specRef says 'The sentences are plan readings', and its coverage says 'Differences on A-4 templates: 0. T12's non-template sentences: P5-RT-05-04'. Its expected rests on A-4's move rule 'which the build applies through speak in every move template', applied to sentences that are not moves. A-12 concerns rendered mathematics. P5-A2.md records that the formula is MathML (msub, msup) with an aria-label in words, and the lens's own coverage confirms it ('T12's relation formula is a <math> with msub and msup outside .katex, named in words'). A live-region string is not rendered mathematics. The pick sentence's tail is explanation(rep). Its wording is logged in P5-A2.md: 'Node i is minuscule: every number in the orbit of ωi is −1, 0 or 1, and all the relations hold.' ... 'What the specification left open: the wording. Default used: the plan's.' The build matches that record. Lens file section 6 excludes plan readings where A-4 is silent, unless they contradict the A-4 text, and A-4's text covers only moves.
verdicts.reason: the finding applies A-4's rule for move templates ('with negative numbers spoken as minus') and A-12's rule for rendering to relation-pick and node-pick sentences that neither passage governs (R2). 7.5 fixes no wording for these results under 4.0 [D], the formula itself is MathML named in words as A-12 asks, and the explanation wording, with its true minus, is logged in decisions/P5-A2.md (R5).
